rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns a constant half4 to attachment zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned RGBA16Float pixel.

name: tanpi-has-poles-at-the-half-integers
rationale: Metal's tanpi is not tan(float(pi)*x). float(pi)*0.5 misses pi/2, so the pre-multiplied form has no pole at all: it returns a large finite number of the wrong sign where Metal returns an infinity. Device-measured over 4091 arguments on an Apple M3 Max, tan(pi*x) disagrees with tanpi on 3184; sinpi(x)/cospi(x) disagrees on 98, none by more than 1e-5 relative, and reproduces every row here exactly. The rows are the ones the quotient makes structurally exact whatever the underlying sine and cosine do -- at a half-integer the reduction residue is 0, so the numerator is an exact +-1 and the denominator an exact +0.0 and IEEE division gives the correctly signed infinity; at an integer the numerator is a signed zero and the denominator +-1. Both signed zero arguments, both quarter turns, a large half-integer at 12345.5 where a pre-multiply would have flushed, and the non-finite guard are included. precise::tanpi and fast::tanpi agree on all 4092 measured arguments, so both AIR spellings are exercised in one kernel and must answer identically. Every argument is read from a buffer so nothing folds, and the non-finite row reports isnan rather than a NaN payload. It discriminates on 18 of its 24 rows: run against the pre-multiplied lowering the candidate answers -2.28e7 for tanpi(0.5), +2.28e7 for tanpi(-0.5), -8.38e7 for tanpi(1.5), -96751.9 for tanpi(100.5), +1169.7 for tanpi(12345.5), 8.74e-08 for tanpi(1) and -0.0 for tanpi(-0); only the two quarter turns and the isnan row survive it.

name: amplification-id-zero-drives-the-render-target-array-index
rationale: The harness runs a single view -- validation/src/case.rs rejects an amplification_count other than one -- so [[amplification_id]] is zero at every vertex, and this shader spends it twice: once as the [[render_target_array_index]] it writes and once inside the colour it emits. The observed varying is therefore (1.25, 2.5, 3.75, 5.0), four distinct dyadic rationals exact in binary32, with the amplification id carried by the first lane so that a non-zero read moves it and a swapped lane is visible. The layer write is not incidental. This is the smallest shader that both reads air.amplification_id and writes air.render_target_array_index, which 27 corpus vertex modules do, and that pair is what becomes a SPIR-V ViewIndex input beside a Layer output. Reference SPIRV-Cross renders a second [[render_target_array_index]] member for the ViewIndex and Metal refuses the resulting vertex function, so the pair is exactly the question this case puts to the runtime: layer zero on a single-layer target is the only layer a case can name, which leaves whether the runtime can compile the pair at all as the whole content of the run.

name: bicubic-weight-table-at-every-fraction-on-rgba16-unorm
rationale: The weights of Metal's filter::bicubic at every 1/256 fraction of each axis, read through rgba16_unorm, whose filtered sums Metal rounds to the format's own step (WP-BCU, D234), so a single tap of code 65535 returns its weight W (in units of 2^-16) as code W, or W - 1 above one half. Texture 0 is 8x16; columns 1-4 are the four taps of base column 2 and rows 1, 5, 9, 13 hold the readings, every other row zero: row 1 holds tap 1 alone at codes 65535 and 65534 (channels 0, 1) and tap 2 alone at the same two codes (channels 2, 3); row 5 taps 0+1 and taps 2+3 at the same codes (an outer weight is negative, but each pair's sum is not); row 9 code 32768 on taps 1+2, all four, 0+1+2, and 1+2+3, which also pins the rounding of a tie (an odd weight sum); row 13 random codes. Texture 1 is its transpose, sampled at the swapped coordinate, so each lane reads the same taps vertically. Lane 4k + r samples pixel coordinate (2.5 + k/256, row r + 0.5) for k = 0..255 and the four rows: horizontal fraction k/256 and vertical fraction 0 (whose weights (0, 1, 0, 0) the zero rows around each reading leave unread), through one clamp-to-edge bicubic sampler with pixel coordinates. Lane i writes texture 0's sample to out[2i] and texture 1's to out[2i + 1] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: normalized-packs-where-the-float-product-ties
rationale: How Metal rounds a normalized pack. STATUS wave 11 owes this reading; it decides the pack lowering in src/lower/arith (PackRounding). D57.10 rounds to nearest even. D78.2 rounds the exact product x * (2^N - 1), from the old engine's rgb10a2 measurement, and extends that to every normalized format ('unmeasured for the others'). D110.4 found that rgb565 rounds the f32 product fl(x * m) instead. The 8- and 16-bit formats are unmeasured. Float inputs: for every tie j + 1/2 of m = 255, 127 (both signs), 3, 31, and 63, and for 64 ties each of m = 1023, 65535, and 32767 (both signs), the float within 3 ulps of (j + 1/2)/m whose f32 product with m is exactly j + 1/2 while the exact product is not (every tie has one except j + 1/2 = m/2, where x = 0.5 makes the exact product the tie itself; 0.5 is among the specials). Rounding the f32 product to even and rounding the exact product disagree where j is even and the exact product lies above the tie, or j is odd and it lies below; rounding the f32 product half up differs from rounding it to even where j is even. Half inputs: the halves nearest every tie of m = 255, 127 (both signs), 31, and 63, and 64 of m = 1023, and every half in (0, 1) whose f32 product with 65535 (8 halves) or 32767 (4, both signs) rounds onto a half-integer. A half times an 8-, 10-, 5-, or 6-bit scale is exact in f32, so those halves separate only a product formed in half precision. Both widths also get the specials: signed zeros, the smallest and largest denormals, the smallest normals, +-0.5, +-1, +-(1 +- ulp), +-2, the largest finite, infinities, quiet and signalling NaNs, 0.25, and +-1e-30 (float). Each tie sits in a lane its channel reads: 6-bit ties in y (the rgb565 green), 5-bit ties in x or z, 2-bit ties in w (the rgb10a2 alpha), 10-bit ties in x, y, or z. Everything else is spread over the four lanes, so every input is also read by every other format. Padding is 0.25. Thread i writes words 18i..18i+17. For in[i]: unorm4x8, snorm4x8, unorm2x16 of xy and of zw, snorm2x16 of xy and of zw, unorm10a2, unorm565 of xyz (zero-extended), and srgb_unorm4x8 (whose alpha is a linear 8-bit channel). Then the same nine for hin[i]. D57.10 predicts NaN -> 0, snorm -0.5 -> -64 (8-bit) and -16384 (16-bit), rounding the magnitude to even.

name: truncating-zero-extending-fusing-and-clamping-at-once
rationale:
Five uncovered air.* families in one invocation -- air.convert.u.v4i8.f.v4f32, air.convert.s.v3i32.u.v3i16, air.convert.f.v2f16.u.v2i1, air.fma.v3f16 and air.fract.v3f16 -- 39 corpus sources between them and no authored case for any. Every one of the fifteen words was derived by hand before the GPU was asked, and every one came back as derived.

Three of the fifteen are the ones that would catch a wrong lowering; the rest hold the ordinary path beside them.

uchar4(3.9) is 3. A float-to-integer conversion TRUNCATES toward zero; a lowering that rounded answers 4, and the 254.5 lane beside it answers 255 rather than 254. Those two are the whole point of the first four words -- 0.0 and 200.0 are exact either way.

int3(ushort(65535)) is 65535. The AIR name says the source is unsigned and the destination signed, so the widening is a ZERO extension; a lowering that sign-extended answers -1 here, which is the single most likely way to get this family wrong. 40000 has its top bit set too and would answer -25536. 0 is the control that both readings agree on.

fma(1025, 0.9990234375, -1024) is -0.0009765625, and this is the lane that proves the multiply-add is FUSED at half width. The exact product is 1024*(1 - 2^-20) = 1023.9990234375, which a half cannot hold: rounded to half it becomes exactly 1024, and an unfused multiply-then-add therefore answers 0. Only a single rounding of the whole expression keeps the -2^-10 residue. The other two fma lanes are controls where fused and unfused agree, one of them exactly (2*3+1 = 7).

fract(-0.0001220703125) is 0x3bff, the largest half below 1, not 1.0. x - floor(x) is 0.9998779296875 there, which rounds UP to exactly 1.0 in half, so fract must clamp; a lowering that emitted the subtraction alone answers 1.0, which is outside fract's range. The 1.5 and -0.25 lanes beside it are the ordinary path and the negative-argument path, 0.5 and 0.75.

half2 of a bool2 is 1.0 and 0.0, the only two values that family can produce.

The sixteenth word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: loads-and-stores-past-a-device-buffer-by-its-address
rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D225, the device address form): buf's address is converted to an integer, so the product reaches buf by its device address. idx = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 17, 63, then 4, 6, 9, 12, 30, 44, 50, 63. Thread t loads buf[idx[t]] into out[t] (threads 4 to 7 load past buf's 16 bytes, within its 256-byte reach, results Metal leaves undefined: out bytes 16 to 31 are the declared out-of-bounds reads of buf), writes the low four bits of that element's address to out[8 + t] (4 * idx[t] mod 16 on a 16-aligned allocation: 0, 4, 8, 12, 0, 4, 4, 12), and stores 0xA0000000 | t to buf[idx[8 + t]], every store past buf's end (words 4 to 63, within its reach). The output is out: buf's four words, the four reads, then the address bits.

name: stores-past-a-device-buffer-by-its-address-leave-it-unchanged
no_effect: Every store lands past the observed buffer's end, so its authored words are unchanged.
rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D225, the device address form): buf's address is converted to an integer, so the product reaches buf by its device address. idx = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 17, 63, then 4, 6, 9, 12, 30, 44, 50, 63. name: simd-all-and-any-in-a-vertex-function-of-64-points

name: add-a-bias-the-weight-buffer-addresses-in-bytes-to-one-gate-dot-product
rationale:
MPS's multi-input RNN gate reduction, 343 lines, the smallest of 25 corpus hosts of `native/emitter/body/gep_provenance.rs::emit_byte_view_scalar_gep` and the first authored case to reach it. The rule fires four times here: the kernel reaches its per-gate bias by casting the `device float *` weight buffer to `device char *`, offsetting by `wSize.y * wRowStrideInElems` BYTES, and casting back to `float *` -- an element index scaled into a byte offset in the index's own integer width, which is exactly what the rule is for.

One threadgroup of one thread, so `threads_per_threadgroup >> 1` is zero and the cross-lane reduction over threadgroup memory is skipped by its own guard; `nResults` is 1, so the input-vector switch selects `inVec0` once; `wSize.x` is 1, so the dot-product loop runs a single float4 step. The weight row is (1, 2, 4, 8) and the input vector (1, 1, 2, 2), giving lane products 1, 2, 8 and 16 -- distinct powers of two whose horizontal sum, 27, is exact in float under any association and under FMA contraction. `wRowStrideInElems` is 16 and `wSize.y` is 1, so the bias is read from BYTE 16 of the weight buffer, which holds 16.0, and the answer is 43.0. Float 5 of that buffer holds 1000.0 and every unread buffer holds 777.0 or 555.0, so an off-by-one bias offset or a wrong switch arm would be loud rather than silent. The selected region is four times the written footprint: only the first float may change, the other twelve bytes must still be 0xAB. Every params byte outside the six fields the kernel loads is 0xCC.

`authored_bounded`: the input-vector loop runs `nResults` (1) times, the dot-product loop steps by `threads_per_threadgroup.x` (1) from zero while below `wSize.x` (1), so once, and the reduction loop is not entered at all. All three bounds are authored literals no input can change.

name: srgb-decode-of-every-byte
rationale: Metal's sRGB decode at every step it can produce. D110.5 lowers air.unpack.unorm4x8.srgb as the 12-bit table step: k = rint(decode(b / 255) * 4095), then k / 4095 correctly rounded. Only steps 1, 1024, and 4095 were observed (case srgb-transfer-and-its-twelve-bit-table, c91d5b1b); correct rounding at the other steps is expected, not observed, and the rest comes from the old engine's measurement over 256 bytes, which has no committed observation. A byte reaches 256 of the 4096 steps. This case decodes every byte in every color channel: red t, green 255 - t, blue t ^ 0x5a, alpha (7t + 3) & 255, for t = 0..255. Each byte goes to float (air.unpack.unorm4x8.srgb.v4f32) and to half (.v4f16), so the observation holds every step the conversion can produce, in both widths. Thread t writes words 6t..6t+3 (the float lanes) and 6t+4..6t+5 (the half lanes, x in the low half of the first). D110.5 predicts for each color byte b the f32 nearest k / 4095 and the half nearest it, and for alpha the linear b / 255. Compiled with the default fast math, as the corpus's unpacks are.

name: a-narrowing-store-into-a-thread-local-slot-keeps-its-high-bytes
rationale:
`store float` through a pointer whose declared pointee is a 64-bit thread-local slot. Logical SPIR-V has no partial store, so `emitter::body::vector_store::emit_scalar_narrowing_store` lowers it as a read-modify-write: load the slot, clear its low `object_bits`, OR in the zero-extended object, store back. That is only byte-faithful if the high four bytes come through untouched, and nothing else in the store checked it -- the function had no authored case. Measured with per-function coverage against every cased source, this fixture reaches it and no cased source does.

Two things about the shape are load-bearing and both were measured, not guessed. A scalar local is scalar-replaced by the frontend and the reinterpret never reaches the emitter at all, so the slot has to be an array with a DYNAMIC index. And the natural MSL spelling -- `union Slot { ulong u; float f; }` -- does NOT translate: a union lowers to a one-member LLVM struct, so the store's pointee is a `TypeStruct` rather than the scalar the rule requires, and the module is refused with `owned Store violates its pointer-pointee and value-type contract: ... points at %6 (TypeStruct %5), but the stored value is ... TypeFloat 32`. The reinterpreting cast `*(thread float *)&s[j]` keeps the pointee scalar. That refusal is a real gap with corpus reach zero; this case is the spelling that does reach the rule.

The answer is derived, not blessed. Thread t writes 0xdeadbeefcafebabe into slot `in[t] & 1` and 0x0123456789abcdef into the other, then narrows a float over the first slot's low half. So the three words per thread are bits((float)t + 0.5), then 0xdeadbeef, then 0x89abcdef: 0x3f000000, 0x3fc00000, 0x40200000, 0x40600000, 0x40900000, 0x40b00000, 0x40d00000, 0x40f00000 for the first. The second word is the assertion -- a read-modify-write that clears the wrong half, or a full-width store, changes it. The third proves the dynamic index picked one slot and not both: the neighbour keeps its own low half. Every input is exactly representable in binary32 and the output buffer starts all-zero, which no arm can produce.

`loop_free`: no loop and no call. One threadgroup of eight threads, the length of the input.

name: sample-one-of-32-textures-per-fragment-through-one-constexpr-sampler
rationale: DESIGN D299: a fullscreen draw into an 8x4 rgba16_float target. Pixel (x, y) samples element (x + 8y) & 31 of the 32-texture array at [[texture(0)]] through a constexpr linear, clamp-to-edge, normalized sampler at (0.5, 0.5), implicit LOD (sampler.sample_hoisted_grad.switch). Each element is a 1x1 rgba16_float texture of one level, so the sample at its centre has bilinear weights (1, 0) over one clamped texel and the LOD selects the only level: element k reads exactly (k, 100 + k, 16 - k, 0.5), every value exact in half and none a negative zero, whose sign a filter may not keep. So target(x, y) = (k, 100 + k, 16 - k, 0.5) with k = x + 8y, each pixel naming its own element. Where the profile has fewer than 32 samplers per stage the translator samples 32 separate textures through one separate sampler; this case is that form's observation. The observation is the whole target, initially 0xab. The AIR has no loop.
